data.text: CTL-T01 at 7.6 is 2.7 above (+2.7) the 4.9 mean given for the closest cases FCRM-2026-0118, FCRM-2026-0097, FCRM-2026-0084, FCRM-2026-0109 and FCRM-2026-0076. The pack gives no individual ratings, so no range is shown. The analyst should explain what in the evidence supports this deviation, or reconsider the rating against that evidence.

CTL-T01 relies on a DD report audited 2023-11-15. Code flags it stale (more than 24 months before the case), and its stated domestic scope does not cover the MX corridor change. The analyst should explain why this artefact still supports the rating, or reconsider it with current evidence that covers the corridor.

CTL-T04 (rating 8.4) relies on a sampling programme report dated 2026-06-18 that covers existing partners only. It does not cover the new partner or channel in this change. The analyst should explain the coverage, or reconsider the rating with evidence that covers the new partner.

CTL-P01 (rating 7.5) relies on a limits configuration dated 2026-04-22 that was reused from case 0118. Its scope may cover a different product or change, not this one. The analyst should confirm that it applies to this change or provide evidence specific to it.

CTL-G02 (geography, EDD procedure and sample) has a rating of 9.4. That is 2.5 above the given precedent mean of 6.9 (+2.5). The pack does not list the precedent case ids or the range. The analyst should explain why the EDD evidence supports this rating, or reconsider it using the EDD procedure and sample dated 2026-03-02 and the precedent cases from research record #3.

CTL-T01 (channel) has a rating of 6.8 and relies only on a DD report dated 2023-11-15. The code marks this evidence as stale (more than 24 months before the case). The analyst should get current due-diligence evidence or explain why the 2023 report still reflects the control.

The CTL-G03 rating of 6.6 relies on a screening test report dated 2023-02-04. The code flags this as stale because it is more than 24 months before the case. The proposal does not show that this test still reflects how the control works now. The analyst should explain why the old report is still enough, or reconsider the CTL-G03 rating using current evidence.

R-7 broken. The code's detail line reads: "planned control(s) in the scored set: CTL-G04". CTL-G04 (geography, evidence: regulator confirmation letter, 2025-12-09) is marked planned:true but is rated 6.7 and sits in the scored set behind composite 9.2 (record #5). The analyst should explain why a planned control is included in scoring, or take it out of the scored set.

CTL-T01 (channel) is rated 5.7 on a DD report dated 2023-11-15. The code flags this evidence as stale (more than 24 months before the case). The analyst should get current due-diligence evidence, or explain why the 5.7 rating still holds on this report.

CTL-P06 is rated 8.5 based on its 'review calendar and last report', dated 2023-03-09. The code flags this evidence as stale because it is more than 24 months older than the case. The rating may not show how the control works now. The analyst should get current evidence of the periodic review and reconsider CTL-P06 with it, or explain why the 2023 evidence is still enough.
